neighbours.label: The Lisp family of languages and its parenthesized prefix syntax (Lisp, Emacs, Scheme, Clojure, s-expressions), vs other programming languages including other functional ones
fire: My first programming class used Scheme and the book about interpreters.
He configures everything about his editor in a long Emacs init file.
Racket is a descendant of Scheme with a big standard library.
Common Lisp macros can rewrite code before it is compiled.
To sum a list you can write (reduce #'+ '(1 2 3)) at the prompt.
Our backend team switched to Clojure because they liked immutable data.
The interpreter reads each s-expression and evaluates it in turn.
She wrote a small parser in Lisp during the winter break.
quiet: My first programming class used Python and a book about algorithms.
He configures everything about his editor in a long JSON settings file.
Kotlin is a descendant of Java with a modern standard library.
Rust macros can rewrite code before it is compiled.
To sum a list you can write sum([1, 2, 3]) at the prompt.
Our backend team switched to Go because they liked fast builds.
The interpreter reads each statement and executes it in turn.
She wrote a small parser in Haskell during the winter break.

predictions: Lisp, Emacs, Scheme, Clojure, Racket and s-expression code 0.5-1.0; Python, Java, Haskell and Rust in the same framing under 0.06.
